en_US.title: Audio Transcript Censor Rules
en_US.scanner: Damaged audio can hide truth, but subtitles must still serve the player.
en_US.field_note: Diegetic censor marks can hide missing route facts; critical accessibility text stays readable.
en_US.terminal: TRANSCRIPT RULE: damaged words may mask names, payloads or timestamps. Core warning, objective and route-critical text must remain readable.
en_US.audio: Static may hide the name. It cannot hide the alarm.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Audio Transcript Censor Rules balance noir redaction with accessibility and localization.
en_US.external_site: Audio Transcript Censor Rules balance damaged recordings, redacted names, readable warnings, and localization clarity.

en_US.scanner: An image earns release only when it shows evidence object, route, tool, creature sign, or pressure state.
en_US.field_note: Every image brief needs spoiler tier, primary evidence object, scalable presentation note, and crop-safe text boundary.
en_US.terminal: IMAGE GATE: no decorative generic sci-fi. Image must expose route, tool, ledger, pressure state, creature evidence, or public-safe moon and ship context.
en_US.audio: Pretty is not a proof artifact.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Evidence Image Release Rules keep imagery tied to route, tool, ledger, pressure state, creature evidence, moon, or ship context.
en_US.external_site: Public imagery should sell beauty and evidence together: real ocean, readable object, pressure state, and no generic sci-fi decoration.

en_US.in_game_wiki: Native Language Release Rules make every language a shipping artifact, not a machine-translated afterthought.
